headline: Staff present proposed 900-megawatt data center on Unified site, with 10 buildings planned through 2033
summary: The developers, Unified Global Packaging Group and the Kraft Group, propose two Phase 1 buildings of about 250,000 square feet and 90 megawatts each, possibly opening in 2029. Staff's preliminary estimates show approximately $10.4 million a year in property taxes by FY 2031 and just under $28 million at full build-out in 2035. Next steps include a community benefits agreement, a zoning bylaw, and public sessions, with updates at each stage. The board also approved a regional animal control agreement and let a Shaw Farm community garden move to its next stage.
decisions: Approved the town manager entering an animal control intermunicipal agreement with Blackstone and five other towns, 5-0.
Approved letting the Shaw Farm community garden proposal move to its next stage, with final approval later, 5-0.
Approved the 2026 holiday hours for alcohol license holders, 5-0.
Approved the 2027 Select Board meeting schedule as presented, 5-0.
discussion: Data center public comment: Speakers raised concerns about water use, power demand, noise, heat, health, and home values. Many urged the board to stop the project.

Data center next steps: Board members said they want a zoning bylaw, a peer review paid by the developer, and protections for noise, water, and abandonment. The chair said the project is at the start of the process, and voters would decide any final question at town meeting.

Shaw Farm garden site: Members asked that the site be checked for bobolink nesting, the cross-country course, and parking. The community development director said the old well needs Board of Health review and water testing.

Animal control fees: Questions covered which animals the service handles and fees for stray pets. The animal control officer said state law sets a fee of $40 per calendar day for held animals, with fees waived for medical and mental health holds.

Town property authority: Board members discussed how the town charter gives the town manager discretion over town property, and which uses should come to the board first. The board may take up the question at a future meeting.
